title: Configure an SRv6 locator
text: segment-routing / srv6 / locators / locator MAIN / micro-segment behavior unode psp-usd / prefix fcbb:0:4::/48. Defines an SRv6 locator with a /48 prefix; a uN (node) SID is allocated from the locator block. Flex-algo locators (e.g. LATENCY algorithm 128) add algorithm-specific forwarding.

title: Enable IS-IS SRv6
text: router isis <id> / address-family ipv6 unicast / segment-routing srv6 / locator MAIN. Advertises the SRv6 locator in IS-IS so remote PEs install the locator prefix in the RIB (show route ipv6 fcbb:0:4::/48).

title: IPv6 route-reflector for VPN address-families
text: router bgp <as> / neighbor 2011::12 / remote-as <as> / update-source Loopback0 / address-family vpnv4 unicast / address-family l2vpn evpn. Peers an IPv6 route-reflector (RRv6) carrying VPNv4 and L2VPN-EVPN so SRv6-signalled VPN routes are reflected. Verify with show bgp l2vpn evpn summary.

title: Per-VRF SRv6 uDT4 allocation
text: router bgp <as> / vrf <vrf> / address-family ipv4 unicast / segment-routing srv6 / locator MAIN / alloc mode per-vrf. Allocates a uDT4 per-VRF SRv6 service SID for L3VPN over SRv6. VPNv4 routes then carry the uDT4 PSID; show cef vrf <vrf> shows fcbb: forwarding.

title: EVPN-VPWS over SRv6 (uDX2)
text: l2vpn / xconnect group <g> ; evpn / segment-routing srv6 locator MAIN. vpws-seamless-integration keeps the existing LDP pseudowire and adds an EVPN SRv6 endpoint, so the migration is hitless. A uDX2/uDT2 SID is allocated for the L2 service. Verify show l2vpn xconnect and show segment-routing srv6 sid (uDT2).

title: IOS-XE SRv6 flex-algo locators
text: segment-routing srv6 / locators / locator MAIN ... / locator LATENCY algorithm 128 / format usid-f3216. IOS-XE uses flex-algo locators (MAIN/128/129/130). The NSO NED may drop the flex-algo 'algorithm' binding, so on IOS-XE PEs push the locator via a CNC config template with CLI transport.

title: Cisco 8000 egress strict-priority queue
text: policy-map <egress> / class <tc> / priority level 1. Cisco 8000 egress queuing uses 'priority level N' for low-latency strict-priority classes. Lower level is higher priority. Use for voice/real-time traffic-classes.

title: bandwidth remaining percent
text: policy-map <egress> / class <tc> / bandwidth remaining percent <n>. Cisco 8000 egress queuing shares remaining bandwidth among non-priority classes using 'bandwidth remaining percent'. This replaces ASR 9000 'bandwidth percent' in many egress designs.

title: traffic-class matching class-map
text: class-map match-any <name> / match traffic-class <n>. Cisco 8000 egress classification matches on the traffic-class set at ingress, not on DSCP/qos-group. Build egress class-maps with 'match traffic-class' for the queuing policy-map.

title: WRED / random-detect restrictions
text: random-detect (WRED) is restricted on certain Cisco 8000 egress queues depending on NPU/profile. When migrating from ASR 9000, remove random-detect from classes where it is unsupported, or the policy will be rejected. Validate with dry-run before commit.
source: Cisco 8000 QoS Config Guide / Release Notes

title: Single output service-policy per interface
text: An interface accepts only one output service-policy. Applying two egress policies (e.g. a queuing policy and a separate shaping policy both as output) is rejected. Combine into one egress policy-map.

title: qos-group vs traffic-class on egress
text: ASR 9000 designs often 'set qos-group' at ingress and match qos-group at egress. Cisco 8000 egress classification keys on traffic-class. Do NOT carry an egress 'set qos-group' into the Cisco 8000 policy; translate to traffic-class matching.
source: ASR 9000 to Cisco 8000 QoS Migration Notes

title: Ingress DSCP classification
text: class-map match-any <n> / match dscp <values>. policy-map <ingress> / class <n> / set traffic-class <t> / set dscp <d>. Classify on DSCP and set the traffic-class at ingress; the egress policy then queues on traffic-class.

title: Apply input/output service-policy
text: interface <intf> / service-policy input <ingress> / service-policy output <egress>. Binds the ingress classification policy and the egress queuing policy to an interface. Verify with show policy-map interface <intf>.

title: Verify SRv6 SIDs and locators
text: show segment-routing srv6 sid shows uN / uDT4 / uDT2 / uDX2 SIDs and their InUse state. show segment-routing srv6 locator shows each locator Up/Down. show cef vrf <vrf> <prefix> shows SRv6 (fcbb:) forwarding after migration.

title: Remove MPLS/LDP transport
text: IOS-XR: no mpls ldp (and remove mpls oam / ldp interfaces). IOS-XE uses different removal syntax (no mpls ip / no mpls ldp router-id). Remove LDP only after SRv6 cutover (LocPref 150) is verified with zero traffic loss; both transports coexist until then for hitless rollback.

title: RRv6 route-policy local-preference (dual-plane cutover)
text: route-policy RRv6 / set local-preference 50 (dual-plane: SRv6 standby, MPLS preferred) then 150 (cutover: SRv6 best path) / end-policy. Applied to the RRv6 neighbor to shift best-path from MPLS to SRv6 and back (rollback) without reprogramming the data plane.
